_doc: Structural seams per aircraft. Fuselage lines: 'frac' of the length from the nose tip (0) to the tail end (1), or 'at' a landmark (canopy_front, canopy_rear, fin_root_le, wing_root_te, wing_root_le) plus 'offset' in blocks (+ forward). Wing lines: 'chord' fractions from the leading edge, 'span' fractions of the exposed semi-span (root 0, tip 1), 'outer' limits a chord line to span fractions [a, b]. Fin lines work the same way on the vertical tail (span = height).

f_16c.source: F-16 built in three sections (nose, centre, aft); forward splice just aft of the cockpit, aft splice forward of the vertical fin; radome joint; five-spar wing with one-piece skins, leading-edge flap and inboard flaperon (aircraftinformation.info, F-16 structure).

f_15c.source: F-15 fuselage in forward (radome, cockpit, avionics bays), centre (inlets, wing carry-through, main gear) and aft (titanium engine bay) sections; radome joint; three-spar wing with plain flap inboard and aileron outboard (McDonnell Douglas F-15 structure).

su_27.source: Su-27 airframe: nose section (radome, cockpit, avionics bay) joined to the integral centre section behind the cockpit, tail section with engine nacelles and tail booms joined at the wing trailing-edge root; radome joint; leading-edge flaps, flaperons (Sukhoi Su-27 structure, Butowski / Gordon).

mig_29.source: MiG-29 airframe: nose section (hinged radome, cockpit, avionics compartment), centre fuselage with the wing centre section and LERX, tail section with engine bays and tail booms; radome joint; leading-edge slats, flaps and ailerons (Mikoyan MiG-29 structure, Gordon / Butowski).

fuselage.name: nose / centre joint behind the avionics bay
